records.title: Applied AI Architect,  Beneficial Deployments (Life Sciences Community & Enablement)
records.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
records.text: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About Beneficial Deployments Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most. About the Role We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team, focused on helping scientists everywhere get the most from Claude, especially Claude Science. You'll run enablements, workshops and hackathons, build demos that show what frontier models can do for the field, and grow a community of scientists building with Claude. You'll also scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic, so our Applied AI and customer teams can support scientists without you in the room. Responsibilities Be the DRI for scientific enablement: decide what to run, build the materials, deliver them, and measure whether research teams reach daily use of Claude. Lead our programs for activating scientists at scale, such as LSVP and Claude for Researchers: set the goals, design the program and run it. Build demos, notebooks and tutorials that show scientists what frontier models can do in their own work, and be an active voice where scientists share tools online (X, LinkedIn, etc.). Scale scientific enablement inside Anthropic: train our Applied AI and Customer Success teams, and build playbooks they can run without you. Build and lead a scientist community around Claude, and be its ambassador (and support ambassador programs), from small meetups to large conferences. Be the voice of scientists inside Anthropic: turn what you hear into concrete asks and see them through to launch, and partner with Marketing and Comms so campaigns and content reach the scientific community. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have Deep hands-on expertise with AI tools for science such as Claude Science: you know where they shine and where they break. Real credibility as a scientist: hands-on experience doing science in academic labs, biotechs, pharma or research institutes, ideally as a user of the kind of tools you'll help scientists adopt. Experience building or running programs for scientific communities is a plus. A track record of helping many scientific teams adopt a new tool through demos, trainings, workshops or hackathons. Up to date on AI for science, such as agentic analysis and AI co-scientists, and able to explain it to working scientists. Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs: you can prototype a working demo. You don't need to write production code. Clear written and spoken communication: talks, tutorials and docs that scientists find useful. A track record of taking programs or products from idea to results: you set the direction, did the work and were accountable for the outcome, often with no playbook. Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $275,000 — $315,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role Anthropic is looking for a Partner Enablement leader to own how we enable our cloud partner ecosystem. Claude reaches a significant share of enterprise customers through AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, and the sellers, solution architects, and delivery teams inside those organizations are often the first people a customer talks to about deploying frontier AI. This role makes sure they are ready. You will translate Anthropic's product and go-to-market strategy into repeatable programs that help cloud partner field teams find, qualify, and win Claude opportunities, and then deliver them well. That means building the enablement infrastructure end to end: onboarding, launch readiness, sales and technical training, certification pathways, co-sell playbooks, and the metrics that tell us whether any of it is working. The job runs in both directions, and internal enablement is a sizable portion of it. Just as important as readying partner field teams is making sure Anthropic's own GTM organization knows how to work with the hyperscalers: which partnerships we have and what each one actually covers, how co-sell and marketplace mechanics differ across the three providers, when to pull a partner into a deal, and the offering nuances that determine what we can and cannot do through each channel. This is a build role as much as a run role. Cloud partner enablement at Anthropic is early, so you will be designing the operating model at the same time as you are shipping against a fast launch cadence. You will work closely with Partnerships, Applied AI, Product Marketing, Sales, and each hyperscaler's own partner and enablement organizations. Responsibilities You will own the cloud partner enablement strategy across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, defining what "ready" means for each partner motion and building the programs that get partner field teams there. That starts with the co-sell motion: you will build the playbooks that let partner sellers carry Claude into enterprise deals alongside our own team, and you will make sure those assets map to how each hyperscaler's marketplace and co-sell mechanics actually work. You will design and run scalable enablement programs rather than one-off training. That includes onboarding paths for new cloud partner teams, role-based learning journeys for sellers and a repeatable launch readiness motion so partner teams are current on every new model and capability we ship. This work runs in both directions. You will also enable Anthropic's own GTM team, making sure sellers and partner-facing staff know which cloud partnerships we have and what each one covers, how co-sell and marketplace mechanics differ across the three providers, when to bring a partner into a deal, and the offering nuances that shape what we can do through each channel. You will also partner directly with the enablement and partner development teams inside each cloud provider to land Anthropic content inside their channels, which is how this work reaches scale. About the role Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team accelerates the work of organizations doing some of the world's most important under-resourced work: nonprofits, education institutions, scientific researchers, and organizations advancing economic mobility. Education institutions sit at the center of that mission. They train the next generation, they produce the science the rest of the world builds on, and they are structurally short on time, budget, and technical capacity to figure out new technology on their own. You will lead our targeted approach to higher education, with a specific focus on research institutes, research intensive universities, and schools focused on access like community colleges and MSIs. You will also support K12 staff and educators across the globe, in particular in low and middle income countries, where teachers and school staff are the users and the district is often the buyer. Where our scaled motion reaches thousands of organizations one to many, this role is the opposite end of the same ecosystem: a deliberately short list of institutions where depth matters, where a lab, a department, or a whole campus adopting Claude changes what science gets done, and where the buying process runs through provosts, research offices, district superintendents, procurement, grant budgets, and security review. Reach comes first, and commercial results follow from it. That ordering is deliberate and it is shared across every leader on this team: a research institute that adopts Claude to move its science faster is a win on its own terms, and you will be measured on creating that value with the institutions that matter most, not only on pipeline. You are the single accountable owner for the research and education Enterprise book globally: its target list, its AEs, its numbers, and its field voice inside Anthropic. You are half seller, half domain translator. You will personally run the most complex institutional deals, and you will be credible in a room of scientists and educators. You know how research is funded, how a university decides, and what it takes for an education sales motion to land in a software company. You will bring that knowledge to the product, applied AI, and marketing teams who build for this audience. This is a player coach seat. You will be directly involved in deals and directing the account executives who cover education today, and the role is expected to grow thoughtfully with more AEs in key regions globally. Key responsibilities scientific discovery and economic access, support for K12 staff and educators Serve as the lead on our most complex institutional deals — setting the pursuit strategy, opening doors with lab and research-office leadership, university provosts, and personally resolving the toughest hurdles: procurement, security review, and grant-funded budgets. Direct and coach the account executives working education accounts today: joint account plans, deal reviews, and a repeatable motion for landing a university and expanding within it. Build the institutional playbook: how an institute goes from a pilot to a working deployment across a department, what good adoption looks like, and when to bring in applied AI, customer success, or partners. Own the book's numbers, institutions reached, activated, and expanded against goals, and use them to decide where the effort goes next. Work in lockstep with our PLG 1:many motion, so that an institution moves cleanly between scaled programs and direct coverage in both directions. Minimum qualifications Education or research sales. You have sold software as a service into universities, research institutes, or academic medical centers, and you have personally closed complex institutional agreements involving procurement, security review, and multiple decision makers. Science or education background. Sales leadership. You have led a sales business end to end and been the accountable owner for its results, whether as a team lead, a player coach, or the sole owner of a strategic book. Preferred qualifications Global education landscape: experience selling to universities, research institutes, or school systems in more than one region, an understanding of how funding and procurement differ from country to country, and comfort working across time zones with regional teams. Experience with research funding: grants, indirect costs, and how a fixed annual budget shapes what an institution can buy. Track record landing an institution wide agreement at a research intensive university, and expanding from a single department to a campus or system. Familiarity with how AI is already used in research settings and K12 classrooms, and a point of view on where it should go next. An impact, education, research, or mission driven go to market background, and genuine interest in these institutions' constraints. A daily working habit with Claude, and agentic workflows you have built for yourself. About the Team

The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact.

We work alongside public servants to move from initial exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI. Our work combines hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, community, content, and practical transformation tailored to government missions and operating environments.

By translating the potential of OpenAI’s technology into better individual workflows, stronger teams, and improved public services, we help government customers deepen adoption, build lasting organizational capability, and spend more time on mission.

About the Role

The Enablement Lead, Government is a specialist role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. This role is responsible for designing and delivering experiences that support repeatable adoption frameworks, drive sustained activation, expand the breadth and depth of usage, and produce measurable value for government organizations.

This role sits at the intersection of enablement, education, adoption, community, content, and customer experience. It blends strong product fluency, instructional design, customer advisory, and a deep understanding of public service. You will lead live workshops, deliver enablement programs, and design adoption interventions for audiences ranging from front-line public servants and technical practitioners to senior government leaders.

You will be a trusted guide to government customers, helping them learn, share, teach, celebrate successes, and use AI confidently in their day-to-day work. You will help organizations understand not only what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to apply them safely and effectively while respecting their missions, operating environments, workforce needs, and responsibilities to the public.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, supporting successful launches and deployments, and helping government organizations translate product capabilities into tangible mission outcomes. You will own outcomes related to activation and sustained usage while helping shape how OpenAI enables and supports public-sector customers at scale.

This role is based in San Francisco or Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents, helping define effective patterns for responsible adoption across government organizations.

  • Lead government customers through the full enablement lifecycle, from initial onboarding and activation through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

  • Define and manage structured enablement and deployment programs with clear goals, milestones, owners, and measures of success.

  • Design and deliver high-impact engagements—including onboarding sessions, advanced capability training, executive briefings, academies, hackathons, listening sessions, and hands-on mission or workflow labs—for audiences ranging from senior leaders to front-line staff.

  • Guide government leaders, champions, technical teams, and working teams through organizational change by building confidence, establishing effective habits, and translating product capabilities into practical workflows and mission outcomes.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert for designated products, roles, or government mission areas, building deep expertise and identifying emerging public-sector use cases for new product capabilities.

  • Develop government-specific learning journeys, training materials, playbooks, FAQs, demonstrations, use cases, customer impact stories, and communications that enable high-quality adoption programs to scale.

  • Provide timely education for product launches, new features, and capability rollouts, translating product updates into clear and practical relevance for government users.

  • Advise government customers on workforce communications and engagement strategies that build awareness, confidence, participation, and sustained use.

  • Build trusted relationships with government leaders, program owners, technical teams, champions, and front-line public servants, creating experiences that reflect an understanding of their constraints, motivations, and responsibilities to the public.

  • Support government customer communities, events, and peer-learning experiences by keeping resources, discussions, updates, and thought leadership useful and current.

  • Identify and amplify government champions, creative use cases, and meaningful customer outcomes that encourage responsible experimentation, recognize public servants’ contributions, and help other organizations learn.

  • Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Delivery, Product, Global Affairs, Communications, Marketing, Readiness, and other teams to deliver cohesive experiences for public-sector customers.

  • Gather and synthesize government customer feedback, adoption signals, participation data, and engagement outcomes to improve enablement programs and bring the voice of public servants back to Product and other internal stakeholders.

  • Identify patterns across government customers and translate them into scalable programs, content, playbooks, and best practices without losing the human connection required to support public servants effectively.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 6+ years of experience in customer-facing, enablement, instructional, adoption, or transformation roles, engaging executive, business, and technical audiences in government or similarly complex enterprise environments.

  • Understand and value public service and can build credibility with government leaders, program owners, technical teams, and front-line public servants.

  • Possess exceptional presentation, facilitation, and communication skills, particularly when translating complex AI capabilities into clear, accurate, and practical value for audiences with different levels of technical fluency.

  • Have experience designing learning journeys and leading workshops, training programs, executive engagements, customer events, or scaled adoption initiatives.

  • Bring strong practical fluency and enthusiasm across ChatGPT, Agents, and the broader OpenAI product ecosystem, with an understanding of how AI can be applied to real-world government workflows.

  • Are a versatile writer and storyteller who can turn complex information into useful and compelling training materials, presentations, demonstrations, communications, and customer stories.

  • Can connect product capabilities and enablement activities to measurable outcomes such as activation, sustained usage, improved quality, faster delivery, reduced administrative burden, better decision-making, risk reduction, customer satisfaction, or mission impact.

  • Can identify patterns across government customers and convert them into scalable systems, programs, content, and best practices.

  • Are highly organized and comfortable managing multiple workstreams, adapting in live customer environments, and bringing clarity and momentum to ambiguous situations.

  • Bring humility, empathy, curiosity, and a genuine desire to help public servants and colleagues succeed.

  • Are personally committed to fostering the safe and responsible evolution of AI.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. records.text: About the Team The Scaling team is responsible for the architectural and engineering backbone of OpenAI’s infrastructure. We design and deliver advanced systems that support the deployment and operation of cutting-edge AI models. Our work spans system software, networking, platform architecture, fleet-level monitoring, and performance optimization. About the Role We’re hiring an SW Engineer to enable production workloads and end-to-end testing on new platforms. This role will include creating new test harnesses and platform stress benchmarks, porting existing inference and training workloads to new, sometimes early-access, systems/hardware, analyzing performance and bottlenecks, and characterizing the end-to-end behavior of new systems (compute, comms, storage, control plane, and failure modes). Key Responsibilities Port and validate key inference and training workloads on new platforms/SKUs as they arrive; drive correctness, performance, and stability to an internal readiness bar. Build a suite of benchmarks and stress tests that capture real E2E behavior of our workloads by exercising all aspects of a system, including CPU, GPU, memory subsystem, frontend, scale-up, and scale-out networking (including WAN traffic, NVlink and RDMA collectives), storage, thermals, and any other relevant parts. Deep-dive performance on distributed training/inference: Collective performance and tuning (across NCCL/RCCL and internal libraries) Overlap of compute/communication, kernel-level bottlenecks, memory bandwidth and scheduling effects Create repeatable test harnesses that run in CI / lab environments and produce actionable outputs (pass/fail, performance score, regression detection). Partner with systems + fleet bring-up engineers to ensure the platform is not only stable and performant, but also operationally usable and scalable (containerization, K8s integration, telemetry hooks, failure triage loops). Work cross-functionally with vendors and internal stakeholders by producing clear bug reports, minimal repros, and prioritized issue lists. Qualifications BS in CS/EE (or equivalent practical experience). 5+ years in one or more of: ML systems, performance engineering, distributed systems, or HPC. The Agent Enablement Applied AI Engineering team works across engineering, product, design, partnerships, and strategic customers to grow an open ecosystem of agent-enabled sites and services. We help partners adopt the OpenAI tech stack related to identity, permissioning, agent-auth primitives so users can safely connect ChatGPT and Codex to the tools, services, and workflows they already use. Our team also works with external partners on defining the standards for agent access, marketplace offerings as well as other agent enablement initiatives to ensure users of ChatGPT and Codex go from intent to task completion seamlessly.

About the role

We are looking for an Applied AI Engineer to help strategic partners design, build, validate, launch, and operate agent enablement integrations across web applications, connectors, APIs, CLIs, MCP servers, and developer tools. This is a hands-on, partner-facing product engineering role for someone who can contribute to the platform itself, lead sophisticated technical engagements, and turn ambiguous identity and agent-workflow requirements into secure, production-ready integrations.

You will work across partner product and engineering teams and OpenAI’s product, engineering, design, partnerships, legal, policy, security, support, and go-to-market teams. You will identify high-value user journeys, choose the right integration path, prototype and review architectures, write code, run evaluations and dogfood, trace failures end to end, guide launch and rollout, and support post-launch iteration. The best person for this role moves fluidly between full-stack code, OAuth/OIDC and identity systems, product judgment, project leadership, and clear communication with engineers and executives.

This role is a fit for a product-minded engineer who wants to stay close to users and partners while going deep on authentication, permissions, reliability, safety, and developer experience. The principle objective is to help partners ship low-friction, trustworthy agent experiences that work across real-world account states, enterprise constraints, and user expectations.

This role is based in our San Francisco office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the technical partner journey for priority agent enablement integrations—from use-case selection and readiness assessment through architecture, prototype, implementation, evaluation, launch, rollout, and ongoing maintenance.

  • Help partners choose and implement the right integration path across browser sign-in, connector-initiated OAuth, and agentic account linking or provisioning, with clear user journeys and safe fallback behavior.

  • Write production and sample code, build reference implementations and test harnesses, and create the technical guidance, integration checklists, evaluations, and debugging tools that move partners from concept to production.

  • Debug identity and agent workflows end to end: user interface state, browser redirects, PKCE/OIDC transactions, token exchange and validation, account mapping, connector callbacks, CLI or MCP handoffs, latency, retries, rate limits, logs, traces, and metrics.

  • Review partner architectures and implementation plans for API contracts, scopes and permissions, consent, terms acceptance, and account policy, secret handling, data boundaries, privacy, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

  • Run hands-on evaluations, dogfood, launch-readiness reviews, staged rollouts, and post-launch investigations; turn findings into concrete fixes rather than one-off workarounds.

  • Contribute targeted improvements to ChatGPT, Codex, and the Agent Enablement platform, including identity protocols, APIs, SDKs, docs, examples, internal tooling, partner-debugging workflows, launch guardrails, and user-facing consent or control experiences.

  • Work closely with product, engineering, design, partnerships, legal, policy, security, support, and go-to-market teams to make partner launches smooth, safe, and repeatable.

  • Bring structured signals from partners back to product and engineering, and turn recurring integration patterns into platform requirements, reference architectures, playbooks, and developer guidance.

  • Have 4–6 years of professional software engineering or AI engineering experience and are strong enough technically to contribute to the platform itself while still enjoying hands-on coding.

  • Have operated in a customer or partner facing roles in scoping projects, building MVPs, presenting trade-offs in solution design and architecture, understanding user value drivers as well as scoping and executing on tight implementation plans.

  • Have built and operated production full-stack products, APIs, backend services, developer platforms, connectors, or integrations, and can reason across frontend, backend, auth, data models, reliability, privacy, and UX constraints.

  • Have a strong understanding of how plugins and connectors work with coding agents, integrating MCP servers, using CLIs and APIs to access external tools.

  • Can work comfortably with external engineers, product leaders, and executives, and translate partner feedback into crisp technical plans and product improvements.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing conditions, and can turn high-level ideas into runnable prototypes, API contracts, technical specs.

  • Balance urgency with judgment and can keep complex partner launches moving while staying precise about the details that matter.

Preferred qualifications:

  • High-level understanding of the identity stack, including how OAuth works.

  • Experience designing or operating APIs, webhooks, schemas, SDKs, CLIs, MCP servers, tool-calling systems, or other developer-facing integrations.

  • Prior customer-facing or partner-facing engineering experience, including leading technical calls, navigating ambiguity, and helping external teams ship production software.

  • Strong familiarity with AI products, LLM APIs, ChatGPT or Codex surfaces, coding harnesses, developer platforms, agent workflows, or ecosystem products.

For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information.   • Own the target architecture for enterprise software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, and agent-enabled business systems across Corporate IT. Drive deprecation and consolidate targets for enterprise software.

  • Create architecture standards for identity, access, data movement, API usage, admin rights, auditability, observability, and vendor integration.

  • Partner with Security to ensure software architecture addresses SSO, SCIM, MFA, privileged access, non-human identities, secrets, token storage, data residency, encryption, retention, and incident response readiness.

  • Partner with Procurement and Finance to evaluate renewals, rationalization opportunities, enterprise agreements, and build-versus-buy decisions.

  • Partner deeply with application verticals such as GTM, Finance, Legal, HR, Research, Product, and Operations teams to evaluate agentic business workflows and translate them into scalable enterprise system patterns.

  • Review proposed SaaS and internally built tools for overlap, risk, integration quality, ownership, lifecycle, supportability, and long-term fit.

  • Develop reusable architecture blueprints for common capabilities such as intake, workflow, approvals, knowledge management, customer/partner 360, data integration, reporting, content management, learning, surveys, and collaboration.

  • Help define where OpenAI-native GPT or agent-built solutions should replace or enable point SaaS tools.

  • Create clear decision records and architecture artifacts that are understandable by business leaders, engineers, security reviewers, and procurement partners.

  • Drive software catalog maturity by connecting tool inventory, business owner, system owner, integration path, data classification, access model, renewal, risk posture, and support model.

  • SaaS governance and software catalog maturity

  • Enterprise integration architecture, including APIs, event flows, middleware, and system-of-record boundaries

  • Identity, access, and admin model design across internal and external users

  • Data architecture for SaaS, customer, supplier, employee, partner, product, consumption, and connected business models.

  • Agentic workflow architecture and GPT-built replacement patterns

  • Vendor architecture reviews and enterprise agreement leverage across strategic platforms.

  • Security, compliance, ITGC, audit evidence, and operational readiness

  • Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management

What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, business systems architecture, IT architecture, SaaS governance, integration architecture, or a related technical leadership role.

  • Strong understanding of SaaS operating models, software lifecycle management, software asset management, and vendor/platform governance.

  • Experience designing integrations across systems, experience in large scale SaaS such as CRM, ERP and Marketplace platforms.

  • Practical knowledge of identity and access patterns including SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, RBAC/ABAC, privileged admin models, service accounts, OAuth apps, and token governance.

  • Ability to evaluate software from multiple angles: business value, architecture fit, security posture, data exposure, cost, supportability, user experience, and vendor strategy.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, building structure where little exists, and influencing senior stakeholders without relying only on formal authority.

  • Ability to write clear architecture decision records, governance standards, system diagrams, business cases, and executive-ready recommendations.

  • Strong partner orientation: able to help teams move faster while raising the quality of decisions.

  • Curiosity about AI-native enterprise architecture and where GPT, Codex, and agentic workflows can replace or enable traditional SaaS patterns.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience scaling IT or business systems from startup-stage tooling into mature enterprise architecture.

  • Experience with architecting systems in a high-growth environment.

  • Experience building governance for internally developed tools, low-code/no-code platforms, agents, or employee-built automation.

Employers will gain a clearer view of workforce skills and progress, helping them recognize capability, focus development where it matters most, and build confidence in workforce readiness. About the Role We’re looking for a full-stack engineer to define and build a new class of learning experiences. This is an early-stage product area where technical judgment, product sense, and learner empathy are critical. You will be setting a technical vision for how people use AI to learn how to use AI, safely and beneficially. This is a hands-on, 0-1 product engineering role with broad technical and product ownership. You’ll set direction, make foundational decisions, and ship the first versions of experiences that can grow into the default way people learn at work. You will drive full-stack product experiences end to end, from prototype through launch, instrumentation, iteration, and production hardening. The work spans interaction design, frontend implementation, backend APIs and services, learner state, content and runtime integration, telemetry, evaluation, reliability, safety, accessibility, and launch readiness. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical decisions and tradeoffs to different audiences. Careful judgment when building products that shape how people understand and use AI. You’ll lead focused experiments, measure what helps learners progress and where they struggle, and use that evidence to shape what comes next.

Strong candidates will be product engineers with experience and a strong interest in education, learning science, assessment, behavior change, or AI literacy. You’ll help shape how OpenAI supports structured, adaptive learning in the flow of work, from a learner’s first entry point through practice, feedback, progress, and repeated use.

  • Create reusable components and internal tools that allow education and content partners to develop, configure, test, and improve learning experiences

  • Build and test clear entry points, realistic hands-on practice, useful feedback, telemetry, and evaluation. Use evidence from real use to decide which capabilities for saved context, progress, re-entry, and reuse are needed next.

  • Partner closely with colleagues across Customer Readiness, EDU Engineering, learning science, research, design, data, content, support, and customer-facing teams. Reuse technical and learning patterns where they help while keeping the experience grounded in professional and enterprise use cases.

  • Work closely with design and users to turn product and learning goals into clear requirements, prototypes, milestones, reusable UI patterns, and product metrics, then refine the experience through evidence.

  • Define the learner intent and problem for each release, then use product data, learner feedback, and operational signals to evaluate product quality, learning, transfer to real work, and adoption against that intent.

  • Make pragmatic tradeoffs across speed, quality, scalability, and operational simplicity in a 0-to-1 product area.

Qualifications:

  • Have 5+ years of experience as a software engineer working on applied AI or user-facing systems

  • Former founder, or early engineer at a startup who built a product from scratch is a plus

  • Substantial experience building and operating high-quality user-facing products with a record of staff-level technical leadership and hands-on delivery

  • Strong full-stack engineering skills, including modern frontend technologies such as TypeScript and React, backend services and APIs, relational databases, stateful user flows, and instrumentation, with practical judgment about distributed systems, reliability, and performance.

  • Experience building in 0-to-1 or fast-moving product environments where user needs, product shape, and success measures are still evolving.

  • Strong user empathy and a high bar for product and interaction quality, accessibility, reliability, safety, security, and performance.

  • Experience collaborating across engineering, research, product, design, data, content, operations, and customer-facing teams.

  • Ability to use qualitative feedback and product data to identify friction, prioritize work, and improve outcomes.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical decisions and tradeoffs to different audiences.

  • Careful judgment when building products that shape how people understand and use AI.

You might thrive in this role if:

  • You like 0-to-1 product work where the right answer is discovered through shipping, measurement, and iteration.

  • You are excited by product surfaces that sit close to real users, real workflows, and measurable user and business outcomes.

  • You can move between prototype speed and production-quality engineering without losing sight of the user.

  • You enjoy working with non-engineering partners and turning domain expertise into clear product experiences.

  • You are energized by education, behavior change, skill development, or helping people gain confidence with new tools.

  • You have strong opinions about product craft but can adjust quickly as evidence comes in.

Nice to have:

  • 5+ years of professional engineering experience (excluding internships) in relevant roles at tech and product-driven companies

  • Former founder, or early engineer at a startup who has built a product from scratch is a plus

  • Experience building education, edtech, learning, tutoring, coaching, assessment, onboarding, training, or enablement products.

  • Experience in AI literacy, workforce learning, enterprise enablement, developer education, or similar spaces where users need to build confidence and skill over time.

  • Experience building AI products, LLM applications, developer tools, agent-assisted workflows, or personalized user experiences.

  • Experience building customer-facing, revenue, sales, support, or go-to-market systems where product quality and operational feedback loops matter.

You will build the teams, systems, service model, and cross-functional partnerships that enable sourcing and contracting at scale, helping teams move quickly without losing commercial discipline or accountability. You will partner with GTM, Sales, and Partnerships to develop Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth. Bring procurement-industry knowledge, buyer insights, and lessons from internal AI use into customer engagement, product feedback, and opportunities across the procurement ecosystem. About the team

The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation (AIT) team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact. We work alongside government leaders and public servants to move from exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI, including our Cyber and Daybreak capabilities.

Our work combines strategic communications, hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, and community building, tailored to government missions and operating environments.

About the role

We are seeking a Cyber Enablement Lead to help government cyber professionals turn Daybreak’s capabilities into stronger defenses and measurable mission outcomes. This role combines technical credibility, hands-on teaching, strategic communication, and cross-functional leadership.

You will own Daybreak’s government product enablement strategy and personally design and deliver the training that brings it to life. Your work will span audience research, curriculum design, recorded demonstrations and courses, hands-on workshops, executive briefings, and cyber councils. You will work directly with U.S. and international government cyber leaders to translate frontier AI capabilities into practical workflows that address operational challenges.

You will also partner with the cyber product team, bringing customer feedback, deployment challenges, and adversarial context into product development. Your work will help shape best practices for adopting and deploying our cyber tools, strengthen government cyber defenses, and inform the direction of these capabilities.

You will engage across the government cybersecurity ecosystem, including Authorizing Officials (AOs), CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior executives. Practitioners need practical proficiency; executives need a strategic understanding of our cyber products, their value, and their implications for mission and risk. Success means demonstrated capability, sustained adoption, and better cyber outcomes.

This role is based in Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required.

In this role, you will

  • Set the vision and own the execution of Daybreak’s government enablement strategy, from audience research and learning objectives to curriculum, delivery, and measurable mission impact.

  • Serve as a trusted cyber ambassador for OpenAI, leading substantive conversations about our tools and capabilities with U.S. and international government leaders, customers, and the broader cyber community.

  • Help government leaders understand and respond to AI’s changing cyber landscape through executive briefings, public speaking, and thought leadership grounded in operational experience.

  • Personally lead technical training, live demonstrations, hands-on workshops, and executive conversations that help AOs, CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior leaders apply Daybreak to their work.

  • Bring frontline experience into product development. Serve as a key point of contact for Daybreak Blue and Red, translating user feedback, deployment friction, and unmet mission needs into actionable product recommendations.

  • Create practical learning materials, including scripts, recorded demonstrations, interactive labs, digital courses, videos, facilitator guides, and playbooks.

  • Convene and lead our cyber councils, bringing leaders and practitioners into candid conversations that surface hard questions, share field lessons, and build a community of practice.

  • Deliver tailored engagements for specialist teams and repeatable learning programs that equip thousands of practitioners to use Daybreak effectively.

  • Translate frontier capabilities into practical government workflows across the cybersecurity lifecycle, connecting Daybreak’s applications and deployment requirements to challenges such as critical infrastructure security and defense of critical networks.

  • Develop practical guidance for human-machine teaming in cyber, including where AI adds value, where human judgment is essential, and how teams validate results and act responsibly.

  • Coordinate across product, security, deployment, and customer teams to address adoption barriers and keep enablement technically accurate, operationally relevant, and current as capabilities and requirements evolve.

  • Assess demonstrated proficiency, track sustained adoption, and use evidence of stronger cyber performance and mission outcomes to improve programs.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Hold an active security clearance, preferably TS/SCI

  • Bring deep cybersecurity expertise across threat modeling, vulnerability discovery and validation, prioritization, remediation, detection, incident response, and recovery, with the judgment to connect these disciplines to government missions.

  • Have deep fluency in Daybreak’s capabilities, applications, and deployment requirements, and can translate that knowledge into credible advice and practical government cyber training.

  • Have personally built and delivered cybersecurity enablement that changed how people work, from focused engagements with specialist teams to programs reaching thousands of practitioners.

  • Are a compelling speaker, writer, educator, and hands-on creator. You can set the strategy, write the script, record the demonstration, build the lab, and lead the workshop, roundtable, or private executive session.

  • Can earn trust in executive briefings and technical deep dives, adapting your language, examples, and level of detail while giving audiences a clear reason and a practical way to act.

  • Know how to read a leader and a room. You combine presence and emotional intelligence with humility, listen carefully, welcome hard questions, and make people comfortable learning something new.

  • Understand government cyber missions, security requirements, and operational constraints, ideally across DOW, federal civilian agencies, and state and local government, and can build approaches that work within those realities.

  • Turn ambitious goals into disciplined execution, leading cross-functional work, incorporating feedback, and taking ownership of demonstrated proficiency, sustained product use, and stronger defenses.

  • Have built and led teams of cyber enablement professionals, setting a high bar for technical credibility, teaching quality, and execution while helping others grow.

  • Bring a practical understanding of U.S. cybersecurity laws, regulations, and policies, and can explain their implications for government adoption and deployment.

  • Have served in a government cyber role and bring a deep commitment to the people behind the mission, including public servants, warfighters, and the intelligence community.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. records.text: Who We Are Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About the Role: As Notion’s product surface expands, we need a builder-teacher who can turn new capabilities into technically accurate education that helps customers confidently build with Notion. In this role, you’ll explore Notion’s newest capabilities, teach by showing, and ship as the product evolves. You’ll be the technical face of Notion Academy: leading workshops, recording walkthroughs, and building implementation guides. This role is based in New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Expand Notion’s technical education library. Author technically rigorous Academy content, implementation guides, and Help Center resources that make our most complex capabilities easier to understand and adopt. Become a trusted voice for Notion Academy. Teach customers through video, live webinars, and workshops, demonstrating real workflows and solving problems in real time. Build with Notion’s newest capabilities. Get hands-on with new product features, use customer insights to identify high-value use cases, and determine top priority workflows for education to focus on. Reimagine learning with AI. Experiment with adaptive, contextual learning experiences that respond to what customers are trying to build and where they need help. Prove and scale the impact of technical education. Use product adoption signals to measure impact and improve what we teach, then build reusable standards to help the team deliver effective technical learning faster. Skills You'll Need to Bring: Builder mindset: You learn new product features by getting hands-on, experimenting, and building until you understand. Comfort navigating technical content: you don’t need to write code, but you can read a technical architecture doc, identify what’s outdated, and work with engineers to fix it. Customer-facing credibility: You’re comfortable teaching, building, and troubleshooting in front of customers. AI experimentation: You actively use AI to build, learn, and teach technical proficiency. Product expertise: You can quickly understand a new feature, identify where it creates meaningful customer value, and turn that into practical use cases. Nice to Haves: Notion product expertise Experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as solutions architecture, sales engineering, developer relations, or technical enablement Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $135,000 - $180,000 per year. By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy and NYLL 144 . #LI-Onsite A Note on AI You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. Equal Opportunity & Accommodations We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. About the Role: Own how our Foundations business teams design, automate, and operate their most important workflows. Notion is growing quickly, and the processes that run our business — intake, triage, execution, approvals, escalations, reporting — need to scale without adding headcount or losing auditability. This role exists to redesign those processes end to end and to embed AI directly into them, so the work moves faster and the system stays trustworthy. What's different at Notion: you'll build on Notion as customer zero. You'll design multi-system workflows spanning Notion, Slack, email, support tooling, and internal data, then ship the custom agents, skills, and automations that run them — partnering with Finance, Legal, People, Ops, Data, and Engineering to drive real adoption, not just documentation. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Redesign cross-functional processes end to end: Map and optimize core and cross-functional flows for Foundations business teams, making them simpler, faster, and more consistent than the operating models they replace. Architect multi-system workflows: Design workflows spanning Notion, Slack, email, support tooling, and internal systems and data, with clear states, routing, permissions, and auditability. original.title: Workflow + Process Designer (AI Enablement)
original.descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About the Role:

Own how our Foundations business teams design, automate, and operate their most important workflows.

Notion is growing quickly, and the processes that run our business — intake, triage, execution, approvals, escalations, reporting — need to scale without adding headcount or losing auditability. This role exists to redesign those processes end to end and to embed AI directly into them, so the work moves faster and the system stays trustworthy.

What's different at Notion: you'll build on Notion as customer zero. You'll design multi-system workflows spanning Notion, Slack, email, support tooling, and internal data, then ship the custom agents, skills, and automations that run them — partnering with Finance, Legal, People, Ops, Data, and Engineering to drive real adoption, not just documentation.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve:

  • Redesign cross-functional processes end to end: Map and optimize core and cross-functional flows for Foundations business teams, making them simpler, faster, and more consistent than the operating models they replace.

  • Architect multi-system workflows: Design workflows spanning Notion, Slack, email, support tooling, and internal systems and data, with clear states, routing, permissions, and auditability.

  • Design for failure, not just the happy path: Identify edge cases, controls, and handoffs so workflows are resilient, reviewable, and easy for a business team to operate without you.

  • Embed AI with clear human-in-the-loop patterns: Define where AI assists, automates, approves, and audits — and make it obvious what AI did and why.

  • Build and maintain custom agents and skills: Ship the agents, structured skills, and runbooks that power intake triage, summarization, routing, escalation, and reporting for business teams.

  • Instrument everything you ship: Define success metrics (cycle time, deflection, quality, adoption), measure them, and iterate based on data and stakeholder feedback.

  • Set the standards others build on: Establish best practices for AI safety, permissions, transparency, and workflow documentation so the patterns hold as more teams adopt them.

  • Drive adoption and change management: Partner with business stakeholders so tooling gets used because it's intuitive and reliable, and measurably improves day-to-day work.

Skills You'll Need to Bring:

  • Process and systems design depth: 2–6 years in operations design, service design, product operations, business systems, or internal tools, with a portfolio showing systems thinking and measurable outcomes.

  • Complex workflow experience: Demonstrated ability to design for intake, triage, routing, approvals, escalations, and reporting across teams and tools, including states, permissions, and auditability.

  • Process mapping rigor: Hands-on experience mapping and improving business processes through journey maps, service blueprints, operating models, and SOPs.

  • AI-native builder mindset: Experience designing or building with AI assistants and agents, workflow automation, or internal tooling — including prompt design, tool selection, and evaluation for quality, reliability, and edge cases. This role requires AI fluency.

  • Lightweight automation ability: Comfort building with Notion custom agents and automations, structured skills, and integrations across systems (APIs, webhooks, connectors). Hands-on preferred.

  • Clear communication and stakeholder judgment: Ability to convey design intent using whatever artifact fits the problem, and to present and defend tradeoffs across multiple tools and teams.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: Experience operating in fast-moving environments and collaborating deeply with engineers and PMs to shape decisions, not just execute them.

Nice to Haves:

  • Consulting background in technology, process and operations consulting, or business/digital transformation — including discovery, current- and future-state process mapping, and stakeholder workshops

  • Track record delivering client engagements across multiple functions or industries, and turning that pattern recognition into repeatable playbooks and operating standards

  • Experience designing internal tools, developer platforms, or enterprise software

  • Familiarity with data concepts (schemas, event tracking, dashboards) and operational analytics

  • Notion product expertise

Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco, the estimated base salary range for this role is $166,000 – $185,000 per year.

By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy.

#LI-Onsite

A Note on AI

You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity & Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Notion is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hello, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.


Where and how you can work

Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under, to a campus in Austin, Texas which is now home to our US operations. This is a hybrid role in Austin, Texas, so you must be able to commute to our office 2 times a week. 
 

About the Team

At Canva, our Higher Education Account Executive team is dedicated to helping educational institutions of all kinds create stunning visual content that inspires and engages students. Our team consists of experienced sales consultants who have a passion for education and a deep understanding of the unique needs and challenges of higher education institutions.

Our Account Executives collaborate closely with colleges and universities to understand how they teach, communicate, and connect. We offer solutions that help faculty share content more easily, help marketing teams reach future students, and help every department create visuals that support learning and growth.

We are committed to building long-term relationships with our customers and providing exceptional customer service every step of the way to help you take higher education institutions to the next level.


About the Role

As a Higher Education Account Executive at Canva, you’ll own our Scaled Higher Education portfolio across the U.S. market, supporting universities with fewer than 5,000 students. You’ll be responsible for driving growth across a broad portfolio of institutions, identifying opportunities to expand Canva’s presence and helping universities adopt and scale the platform across their campuses.

Partnering closely with Customer Success, you’ll manage the university lifecycle from initial engagement and onboarding through adoption, retention, and expansion. You’ll use data and user insights to prioritize opportunities across your territory, build scalable growth strategies, and engage administrators, faculty, and other key stakeholders to drive meaningful adoption.

This role combines high-volume portfolio management with strategic selling. You’ll balance opportunities across the U.S. market, exceed revenue targets, and help establish Canva as a trusted partner for higher education institutions throughout the region.


What you'll do 

As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. This will give you a flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Own the Scaled Higher Education business across the U.S. market. You'll own the strategy, planning, execution, and results for a portfolio of universities with fewer than 5,000 students, identifying and prioritizing opportunities to drive adoption, growth, and revenue across the region.
  • Manage and grow a broad portfolio of universities. You'll build relationships with key university stakeholders and develop scalable sales approaches that enable you to effectively engage and grow multiple institutions across your territory.
  • Drive university-wide adoption. You'll work with administrators, faculty, and other stakeholders to demonstrate Canva's value, navigate the buying process, and support successful deployments across departments, faculty, and students.
  • Build a healthy and predictable business. You'll manage your pipeline and portfolio with a strong understanding of where to focus your time, balancing new opportunities with expansion across existing institutions to consistently deliver against your targets.
  • Understand the Higher Education customer. You'll develop a strong understanding of the needs, priorities, and challenges facing universities across the U.S., and use those insights to position Canva as a valuable partner for teaching, learning, communication, and collaboration.
  • Use data to identify growth opportunities. You'll leverage account, usage, and market insights to prioritize institutions, uncover expansion opportunities, and inform your sales strategy.
  • Partner cross-functionally to scale impact. You'll collaborate closely with Customer Success and teams across Canva to share customer insights, improve our approach to the Higher Education market, and create repeatable strategies that can scale across the region.
     

What we're looking for

  • Experience in Higher Education or Education Technology. You understand how universities evaluate, purchase, and adopt technology and can effectively engage with stakeholders across academic and administrative teams.
  • Strong sales experience. You have experience owning a sales territory or portfolio, managing pipeline, navigating sales cycles, and consistently working toward revenue and growth targets. Experience selling SaaS, education technology, or other technology solutions is highly valued.
  • Scaled portfolio management skills. You're comfortable managing a broad book of business and know how to prioritize your time and opportunities based on customer potential, engagement, and likelihood to grow.
  • A consultative approach to selling. You can uncover customer needs, connect them to Canva's value, and build compelling business cases that resonate with different university stakeholders.
  • Understanding of technology adoption. You understand how institutions evaluate and roll out new technology and can help customers navigate the path from initial interest to broader university adoption.
  • Excellent communication skills. You create clarity by making complex ideas simple and can confidently present, influence, and tell a compelling story to customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Strong business planning and execution. You can translate territory and account insights into clear priorities, execute against a plan, and adapt quickly based on results.
  • Cross-functional collaboration. You enjoy working closely with Customer Success and other teams to deliver a strong customer experience and identify opportunities for growth.
  • Growth mindset. You're curious, adaptable, and eager to learn as Canva's Higher Education business continues to evolve and scale.
     

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll also experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity, and fun woven throughout life at Canva. We also offer a range of benefits designed to set you up for success, both in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages — we want our success to be yours too
  • Health benefits plans to support you and your wellbeing
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents and carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup, and more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge, and support you personally
     

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills, merit and business needs, in compliance with applicable local laws.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

records.title: Product Support Specialist, Education Team  (Full time, 1-year contract)
records.text: Join the team redefining how the world experiences design. Hey, g'day, namaste, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte! Ready to make meaningful impact? You're in the right place. Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point. Every role supporting Canva contributes to something bigger. Here's what this contract opportunity involves and what we're looking for. Where and how you can work This is a 12-month independent contractor opportunity, where you'll provide services within a defined scope, with the flexibility to shape how you deliver your impact. Designed for a hybrid way of working, this opportunity is remote and open to candidates based anywhere in India, so you can align on key touchpoints with our internal team and our education partners across the country. While it'd be up to you to manage your time, the expected time commitment to deliver these services is approximately 40 hours per week. About the team We're the Canva Education team in India, working to bring creativity, collaboration, and visual communication into classrooms across the country. We partner with state governments, national education bodies, and large school networks to make Canva a safe, inclusive platform for teaching and learning — from rural districts to city schools — always aligned with India's priorities like NEP 2020, foundational learning, and digital equity. AI is an accelerant to our mission to empower the world to design. We're embracing it as a powerful tool to help us move faster, spark ideas, streamline work, and unlock creativity. We're genuinely curious about how people are thinking about and experimenting with new technologies to amplify impact, so you can expect it to come up in conversation during the interview process. What you'll be working on As Canva Education continues to grow, change is part of how we move forward. That means the services you'll provide may evolve, and we'd discuss that with you from time to time.
